A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPDiff study. Their text, equations, Tables 1–13, Figures 1–6 and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original computational evaluations of protein-complex and antibody design, including benchmark results, ablations and designed examples in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B and D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original computational evaluations, including the numerical results in Tables 1–5 and 9–13 and the analyses in Figure 2.

M1.justification: The hybrid sequence-structure diffusion model, SSINC architecture, training objective and informative initialization procedure in Section 3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use PPBench, the same ten-target mini-binder dataset, SAbDab antibody tasks and Swiss-Prot pseudo-complex pretraining experiment. Seen-target and zero-shot coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: SEnc+ProteinMPNN, InterleavingDiff and SSINC Network remain in their corresponding comparisons, and RFdiffusion+ProteinMPNN remains in Table 5.

E3.justification: Data splits and sample counts, model configurations, training budgets, AF2/AF3 metrics, success thresholds and candidate-generation procedures match across Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–C.

E4.justification: The causal-attention, diffusion-step, model-scale, Swiss-Prot pretraining and candidate-pool analyses are unchanged. Both also retain the HDOCK analysis and the same designed-complex case studies.

E5.justification: Both retain the same seed descriptions in Sections 5.1–5.3. Neither adds repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. Tables 1–3 retain PPDiff success rates of 50.00% for top-1 PPBench candidates, 23.16% for mini-binders and 16.89% for antibodies.

T1.justification: The problem definition, diffusion distributions, variational derivation, guidance energy and metric definitions in Equations 1–16 are unchanged. Their movement between columns or pages does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same method, dataset and performance claims. The added resource-availability sentence does not revise the core scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the EGFR binding-site explanation and the conclusion's acknowledgment that wet-lab validation is absent.

D1.justification: v2 adds an abstract statement directing readers to the JocelynSong/PPDiff GitHub repository for code, data and models; v1 lacks this project-resource pointer. Implementation and training details in Section 4.2 and Appendix C remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion and positioning relative to previous protein-design and diffusion methods are unchanged. Bibliography differences reflect text reflow.

P1.justification: v2 adds one resource-availability sentence to the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded abstract moves the Introduction opening from the left column to the right column and accompanies subsequent text and equation reflow. Figures and tables retain their content, structure and captions.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer provides a specific location for code, data and models, improving resource discoverability over v1. This is a limited documentation gain: scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, and the supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.
